turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
The highest observed rotating-bending fatigue strengths (1000–1190 MPa) form a tight cluster that uses a carburizing-style schedule (NT = CT = 930, THT = THt = THQCr = 0, Tt = 120, TCr = 0.5, TT \(\approx\) 160) together with a low-carbon Ni-Mo chemistry.  All other heat-treatment families in the data (through-hardening at 825–865 °C, high-C/high-Si grades, etc.) saturate well below 900 MPa, so they cannot be competitive.

Within the carburizing cluster the single best point is
NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5,
C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0
(target 1190 MPa).  Neighbouring points that differ by only a few tens of degrees or a few hundredths of a percent in composition remain above 1050 MPa, indicating a broad plateau rather than a knife-edge.

To keep every coordinate at least 5 % inside the observed box (so that a \(\pm5\%\) perturbation cannot leave the domain) the extreme values Ct=540 and Dt=15 are relaxed to the interior of the same plateau:
